# Format coverage and validation matrix

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/format-matrix-doc.mjs --write` from config/format-matrix.json, the built registry index and
config/derived-exports.lock.json. Do not edit by hand: scripts/test-format-matrix.mjs fails when this file is stale. -->

Which complete-database format each registered dataset offers as a download, where it comes from, how it is checked, and, for every format
that is not offered, why not. The declaration is `config/format-matrix.json`. The build refuses to finish unless the exports it produced are exactly
the declared ones, the declaration is published in each dataset's metadata (`formatAvailability` in `corpus.json` and the page data), and the
dataset and download pages print "Not available: <reason>" for every gap.

Every dataset also offers the SQLite-dialect SQL dump (`sql`, labelled "SQL (SQLite dialect)": it is SQLite syntax, not PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQL Server),

## Not available, and why

- **Northwind, MySQL script.** The pinned fixture is an SQLite conversion of the Access Northwind sample, and the pinned upstream source has no MySQL edition of it. DemoDB has no generator that writes a MySQL script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no MySQL server to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a MySQL dialect to the shared generator (scripts/hosting-tools/postgres_samples.py) and load every dataset into a mysql:8 service container in CI before publishing.
- **Northwind, SQL Server script.** The pinned fixture is an SQLite conversion of the Access Northwind sample; Microsoft's SQL Server Northwind script is a different dataset revision and is not the pinned data. DemoDB has no generator that writes a SQL Server script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no SQL Server instance to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a T-SQL dialect to the shared generator and load every dataset into a SQL Server container in CI before publishing.
- **Pubs, MySQL script.** The pinned upstream source has no MySQL edition of Pubs. DemoDB has no generator that writes a MySQL script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no MySQL server to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a MySQL dialect to the shared generator (scripts/hosting-tools/postgres_samples.py) and load every dataset into a mysql:8 service container in CI before publishing.
- **Pubs, SQL Server script.** Microsoft's instpubs.sql is retained in the provider repository, but the pinned fixture normalises its dates and defaults, so the original script is not the pinned data. DemoDB has no generator that writes a SQL Server script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no SQL Server instance to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a T-SQL dialect to the shared generator and load every dataset into a SQL Server container in CI before publishing.
- **Sakila, MySQL script.** The upstream MySQL Sakila scripts are two files (schema and data) for the original MySQL schema, with triggers, FULLTEXT and SPATIAL objects that the pinned SQLite fixture does not carry, so they are not the pinned data. DemoDB has no generator that writes a MySQL script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no MySQL server to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a MySQL dialect to the shared generator (scripts/hosting-tools/postgres_samples.py) and load every dataset into a mysql:8 service container in CI before publishing.
- **Sakila, SQL Server script.** The pinned upstream source has no SQL Server edition of Sakila. DemoDB has no generator that writes a SQL Server script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no SQL Server instance to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a T-SQL dialect to the shared generator and load every dataset into a SQL Server container in CI before publishing.
- **AdventureWorks OLTP, MySQL script.** The pinned upstream source has no MySQL edition of AdventureWorks. DemoDB has no generator that writes a MySQL script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no MySQL server to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a MySQL dialect to the shared generator (scripts/hosting-tools/postgres_samples.py) and load every dataset into a mysql:8 service container in CI before publishing.
- **AdventureWorks OLTP, SQL Server script.** Microsoft's AdventureWorks installer needs SQL Server features and 68 BULK INSERT files and is not a single script; the pinned fixture is its SQLite conversion. DemoDB has no generator that writes a SQL Server script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no SQL Server instance to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a T-SQL dialect to the shared generator and load every dataset into a SQL Server container in CI before publishing.
- **Employees (browser edition), MySQL script.** The upstream MySQL dump is the full Employees dataset, while the pinned fixture is a documented 1,024-employee subset, so the original script is not the pinned data. DemoDB has no generator that writes a MySQL script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no MySQL server to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a MySQL dialect to the shared generator (scripts/hosting-tools/postgres_samples.py) and load every dataset into a mysql:8 service container in CI before publishing.
- **Employees (browser edition), SQL Server script.** The pinned upstream source has no SQL Server edition of Employees. DemoDB has no generator that writes a SQL Server script from the pinned SQLite fixture and CI has no SQL Server instance to load one into, so an unchecked script is not published. Follow-up: Add a T-SQL dialect to the shared generator and load every dataset into a SQL Server container in CI before publishing.

## Size and hosting

Static assets are limited to 25 MiB per file. A file above that is stored gzip-encoded at level 9 and served decoded by the Worker; if the
encoded stream is still above the limit it is split in `.part` files that the Worker joins (the provider SQLite for AdventureWorks is served that way).
No download in this matrix is partial. Sizes are decoded sizes.

| Dataset | SQLite | PostgreSQL script | JSON | YAML | inGitDB archive |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chinook | 1.0 MiB | 0.6 MiB | 1.8 MiB | 1.3 MiB | ZIP, 29 files, 15,607 rows |
| Northwind | 0.6 MiB | 1.0 MiB | 0.9 MiB | 0.8 MiB | ZIP, 34 files, 3,310 rows |
| Pubs | 0.2 MiB | 0.2 MiB | 0.1 MiB | 0.1 MiB | ZIP, 29 files, 255 rows |
| Sakila | 4.7 MiB | 3.6 MiB | 7.2 MiB | 8.1 MiB | ZIP, 39 files, 47,268 rows |
| AdventureWorks OLTP | 121 MiB (served gzip-encoded) | 105 MiB (served gzip-encoded) | 208 MiB (served gzip-encoded) | 232 MiB (served gzip-encoded) | ZIP, 148 files, 759,240 rows |
| Employees (browser edition) | 0.8 MiB | 0.6 MiB | 1.2 MiB | 1.3 MiB | ZIP, 17 files, 13,584 rows |

The AdventureWorks inGitDB archive is the one download close to the limit; the build fails, rather than publish a partial file, if it ever exceeds it.

## How each format is produced

- **SQLite, per-table JSON and CSV, the SQLite-dialect SQL dump**: provider contract files, verified against the provider checksums pinned in `config/databases.json`.
- **JSON** (generated): `scripts/derived-exports.mjs` joins the provider's per-table JSON arrays, unparsed, as `{"<table>": [rows]}`, so values (exact decimals, base64 BLOBs) are the provider bytes.
- **YAML** (generated): the same rows as block-style YAML. Every scalar is a JSON scalar and numbers are written exactly as in the source JSON.
- **PostgreSQL script**: `scripts/hosting-tools/postgres_samples.py generate` over the pinned SQLite fixture (guarded schema named after the dataset, deferred foreign keys, one transaction).
  Northwind uses its provider's own pinned `artifacts/hosting-imports/postgres.sql`, and Chinook its upstream Chinook_PostgreSql.sql, both provider-checksummed.
- **inGitDB archive**: `scripts/hosting-tools/ingitdb_archive.py` packs the provider's `ingitdb/` directory at the revision pinned in `ingitdbRevisions`, unchanged, after checking its
  export manifest names the same dataset and the same SQLite fixture SHA-256 and records a clean parity check. The inGitDB directory itself is written by DataTug's DALgo to inGitDB export in the provider repository.
- **MySQL and SQL Server scripts**: Chinook's are the unchanged upstream scripts; for the other datasets see the reasons above.

Every generated file is pinned by `config/derived-exports.lock.json` (decoded SHA-256 and size; for the inGitDB archive the digest of its file list), so a change to a generator, an input or an interpreter
that alters a published byte fails the build until the lock is regenerated (`DEMODB_UPDATE_DERIVED_LOCK=1 node scripts/prepare-databases.mjs`, refused in CI) and the diff is reviewed.

## Validation

In every pull request (`pnpm test`, `scripts/test-format-matrix.mjs`, against the built site):

- the declaration, the registry index, `corpus.json`, the rendered pages and the files in the built asset tree describe the same set of downloads, and a served file is within the size limit;
- the complete JSON and YAML of every dataset that has them: table set and order, row counts equal to the schema and to `SELECT count(*)` on the pinned SQLite fixture, every row and value equal to the fixture (BLOBs as base64),
  primary keys unique, every foreign-key value present in the referenced column, and the YAML equal to the JSON (parsed with the `yaml` package for datasets up to 12 MB, and a sample of tables above that);
- this document is current.

In `.github/workflows/served-formats.yml`, against the built asset tree and the provider checkouts at the pinned revisions:

- every served PostgreSQL script is loaded into a throwaway PostgreSQL 17 and compared with the fixture: same tables, row counts, primary-key columns and foreign-key counts, plus the full typed row-multiset check for scripts the shared generator wrote (`validate_served_formats.py`);
- every inGitDB archive is extracted and compared row by row and definition by definition with the fixture by the independent parity checker (`validate_datatug_exports.py`).

After deploy, `scripts/smoke-live.mjs` downloads every complete export listed in `corpus.json` and compares size and SHA-256.

## What remains

- MySQL and SQL Server scripts for Northwind, Pubs, Sakila, AdventureWorks and Employees: needs a dialect in the shared generator and a MySQL and a SQL Server service in CI to verify it (see the follow-ups above).
- The inGitDB archives are validated by the independent parity checker; validating them with the inGitDB CLI in CI needs a CLI release that reads the DataTug 0.61.1 collection definitions (v0.70.0 or newer).
- Formats outside the matrix: sql, metadata are listed in the registry but are not matrix formats.
